summary: Defines the MULTIAPPEND extension to IMAP, letting a client upload several messages to a mailbox in a single operation. This speeds up clients that upload many messages, and servers advertise support with a capability name.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3502 extends the Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) so a client can append several messages to a mailbox with one command. The server either appends every message in that operation or leaves the mailbox unchanged.

questions: how to upload multiple messages with imap
subtitle: Upload multiple messages to an IMAP mailbox with one atomic APPEND command.

tldr.problem: Appending each message with a separate IMAP command can leave a mailbox partly changed if one append fails, and can repeat costly storage work.
tldr.mechanism: MULTIAPPEND lets one APPEND command carry one or more messages, each with optional flags and a date. The operation is atomic: either every message is appended or none is.
tldr.outcome: A server advertises support with the MULTIAPPEND capability. RFC 3502 was later updated by RFC 4466 and RFC 4469.

today: RFC 3502 is a Proposed Standard that was updated by RFC 4466 and RFC 4469. The batch metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: Appending Several Messages Together
sections.content:
The Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) MULTIAPPEND extension changes the APPEND command so it can upload multiple messages in one operation. A server that supports the extension advertises the MULTIAPPEND capability.

When used with the LITERAL+ extension, the upload can take one command-and-response round trip. Most importantly, MULTIAPPEND is atomic: if the operation fails, the mailbox returns to its state before the attempt.
sections.plainLanguage: A client can send several messages to a mailbox using one APPEND command. If any part of that operation fails, none of the messages are added.

sections.title: Why Separate Appends Are Different
sections.content:
In base IMAP, each message uses its own APPEND command. If a client sends several commands in a pipeline, an error on one message does not undo the earlier appends, and later messages may still be appended.

Some mail stores also do costly opening, locking, syncing, and closing work for each append. MULTIAPPEND gives a server one operation to process and avoids the mixed result that can occur when several separate commands fail partway through.
sections.plainLanguage: Several separate commands can leave some messages in the mailbox and others missing after an error. A single MULTIAPPEND operation prevents that partial result.

sections.title: The Multi-Message APPEND Command
sections.content:
The command names a mailbox and then provides one or more messages. Each message may have a parenthesized flag list and a date-time string before its message literal. A successful append returns OK; an append error returns NO; an unknown command or invalid arguments return BAD.

A zero-length message literal is an error and MUST return NO, which can cancel the operation. If the mailbox does not exist, the server MUST NOT create it automatically; it returns an error and may include [TRYCREATE] to suggest that the client create the mailbox and retry.
sections.plainLanguage: Each message in the command can have its own flags, date, and content. If the mailbox is missing or any message makes the operation fail, the server does not create a partial batch.

sections.title: The APPEND Syntax and UIDPLUS
sections.content:
The grammar now allows one or more message arguments after the mailbox name. Each argument consists of an optional flag list, an optional date-time string, and a literal containing the message.

When a server supports both MULTIAPPEND and UIDPLUS, its APPENDUID response returns one UID for each appended message. The returned UIDs follow the order in which the messages were appended.
sections.plainLanguage: The command syntax permits a series of message arguments after one mailbox name. With UIDPLUS, the response can return a matching identifier for each appended message.

sections.title: Security and Status
sections.content:
The extension adds no security considerations beyond base IMAP. The RFC reminds readers that IMAP transactions, including message data, travel in the clear unless protection such as STARTTLS or another mechanism is used.

RFC 3502 is a Proposed Standard that was updated by RFC 4466 and RFC 4469. The batch metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it.
sections.plainLanguage: Sending several messages at once does not protect them from being read in transit. RFC 4466 and RFC 4469 later updated this Proposed Standard.

data.title: ABNF
data.code:
append = "APPEND" SP mailbox 1*append-message
append-message = [SP flag-list] [SP date-time] SP literal
